blocks.text: ח׳ אֶחָד הוּא אֱלֹהֵינוּ הוּא אָבִינוּ הוּא מַלְכֵּנוּ הוּא מוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ. וְהוּא יַשְׁמִיעֵנוּ בְּרַחֲמָיו שֵׁנִית לְעֵינֵי כָּל־חַי לִהְיוֹת לָכֶם לֵאלהִים:
uncertainties: The speaker mark ח׳ is a small superscript.
Possible meteg on יַשְׁמִיעֵנוּ.
לֵאלהִים: the vowels under אלה are unclear, and holam may be absent.

blocks.text: קו״ח אֲנִי יְיָ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם:
uncertainties: Printed centred in large type.

blocks.text: בפֿפֿד״מ אין אומרים כאן אדיר אדירנו.
uncertainties: Rashi script. The first letter could be read as ב or נ. The abbreviation בספר״ם is read as printed, and its exact expansion is uncertain.

blocks.text: ק׳ אַדִּיר אַדִּירֵנוּ יְיָ אֲדֹנֵינוּ מָה אַדִּיר שִׁמְךָ בְּכָל הָאָרֶץ: וְהָיָה יְיָ לְמֶלֶךְ עַל כָּל הָאָרֶץ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יִהְיֶה יְיָ אֶחָד וּשְׁמוֹ אֶחָד:
uncertainties: Small type.
The patah under the first אדיר is faint.
There is a possible accent mark under the first הָאָרֶץ, which is not recorded.

blocks.text: ק׳ תְּהִלּוֹת כְּבוֹדְךָ, אָמְצְךָ מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ. שְׁמָעֲךָ דִּין מִשָּׁמַיִם, בְּכֵן יָרְאָה וְשָׁקְטָה הָאָרֶץ. רַעַשׁ יוֹם מִשְׁפָּט, גָּעֲשׁוּ (נ״א גֵּעַשׁ) תְּהוֹמוֹת הָאָרֶץ. קוֹל שׁוֹפָר חָזָק, דִּבֵּר וַיִּקְרָא אָרֶץ. צְבִי לַצַּדִּיק בְּזֶמֶר, הִשְׁמִיעָה כְּנַף הָאָרֶץ. פַּחַד וָפַחַת וָפַח, וּפַלָּצוּת יַבְעִיתוּ אָרֶץ. עֵת תָּקוּם לַמִּשְׁפָּט, זְעוֹם כָּל אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ. ח׳ סֹלּוּ פַּנּוּ (נ״א סוּרוּ מִנִּי) דֶּרֶךְ יְנוֹבְבוּ, חֲרֵדִים מֵחֶרְדַּת הָאָרֶץ. נָאוֹר וְאַדִּיר, טַעַם תָּשִׁיב לָאָרֶץ. מַה תִּירְאִי אֲדָמָה, יָרִיעוּ תַּחְתִּיּוֹת אָרֶץ:
uncertainties: שְׁמָעֲךָ: the vowel under מ (kamatz or patah, with a possible meteg) is unclear.
Possible meteg on גָּעֲשׁוּ.
The variant reads גֵּעַשׁ or גָּעַשׁ, and the vowel under ג is unclear.
The variant marker is written in small Rashi-style letters. It is read as נ״א but could be read as כ״א.
זְעוֹם: the first letter could be read as ו (וְעוֹם). It is read as ז from the glyph's head and the English 'show anger'.
סוּרוּ in the variant may be unpointed.
There are accent-like marks on אֲדָמָה and טַעַם. These may be meteg or cantillation and are not recorded.
The mid-paragraph ח׳ before סֹלּוּ is printed inline.

blocks.text: קו״ח לְהִתְוַדַּע וּלְהִגָּלוֹת, כִּי הוּא מֶלֶךְ עַל כָּל הָאָרֶץ. כְּמוֹ פֵּאֲרוּהוּ מֵאָז בַּשַּׁחַק, יֻרְשׁוּ בְּחוּנָיו לְפָאֲרוֹ בָּאָרֶץ:
uncertainties: Possible meteg on יִרְשׁוּ, with three dots below that might be a segol. Its vowel is unclear.
A stray hyphen or dot after בְּחוּנָיו is probably a print artifact.

blocks.text: ק׳ אַדִּיר אַדִּירֵנוּ יְיָ אֲדֹנֵינוּ מָה אַדִּיר שִׁמְךָ בְּכָל הָאָרֶץ: וְהָיָה יְיָ לְמֶלֶךְ עַל כָּל הָאָרֶץ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יִהְיֶה יְיָ אֶחָד וּשְׁמוֹ אֶחָד:
uncertainties: Large type. This is a repeated refrain printed in full, not a cue.
The patah under the first אדיר is faint.

blocks.text: ח׳ וּבְדִבְרֵי קָדְשְׁךָ כָּתוּב לֵאמֹר.
קו״ח יִמְלֹךְ יְיָ לְעוֹלָם אֱלֹהַיִךְ צִיּוֹן לְדֹר וָדֹר הַלְלוּיָהּ:
uncertainties: Possible meteg on הַלְלוּיָהּ. The mappiq in the final ה looks present.

blocks.text: ח׳ לְדוֹר וָדוֹר נַגִּיד גָּדְלֶךָ וּלְנֵצַח נְצָחִים קְדֻשָּׁתְךָ נַקְדִּישׁ וְשִׁבְחֲךָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מִפִּינוּ לֹא יָמוּשׁ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד כִּי אֵל מֶלֶךְ גָּדוֹל וְקָדוֹשׁ אָתָּה.
uncertainties: There is an accent-like mark above, between לֹא and יָמוּשׁ. It may be a pashta or a print artifact and is not recorded.

blocks.text: כִּי מַקְדִּישֶׁיךָ בִּקְדֻשָּׁתְךָ (נ״א כערכך) קִדַּשְׁתָּ. נָאֶה לְקָדוֹשׁ פְּאֵר מִקְּדוֹשִׁים. וּבְכֵן יִתְקַדַּשׁ שִׁמְךָ יְיָ
uncertainties: The paragraph continues on the next page and breaks mid-sentence after יְיָ.
No speaker mark is printed. A small dot in the right margin is probably an artifact.
The variant כערכך is unpointed, and its marker is read as נ״א.
Possible meteg on קִדַּשְׁתָּ.

blocks.text: אֱלֹהֵינוּ. עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַמֶּךָ. וְעַל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם עִירֶךָ. וְעַל צִיּוֹן מִשְׁכַּן כְּבוֹדֶךָ. וְעַל מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד מְשִׁיחֶךָ. וְעַל מְכוֹנְךָ וְהֵיכָלֶךָ:
uncertainties: This continues from the previous page, so the start of the sentence is not on this scan.
יְרוּשָׁלַיִם is printed plene, with yod.

blocks.text: עוֹד יִזְכָּר לָנוּ אַהֲבַת אֵיתָן, אֲדוֹנֵינוּ. וּבֵן הַנֶּעֱקָד יַשְׁבִּית מְדַיְּנֵנוּ. וּבִזְכוּת הַתָּם יוֹצִיא אָיוֹם (כ״א היום) לְצֶדֶק דִּינֵנוּ. כִּי קָדוֹשׁ היום לַאֲדֹנֵינוּ: בְּאֵין מֵלִיץ יֹשֶׁר מוּל מָגִּיד פֶּשַׁע. תַּגִּיד לְיַעֲקֹב דָּבָר חק וּמִשְׁפָּט. וְצַדְּקֵנוּ בְּמִשְׁפָּט הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט.
uncertainties: The source variant is printed small and unpointed. It looks like 'כ״א היום', but the first letter could be נ (נ״א). I added the pointing on הַיּוֹם; the print has none.
I can't tell whether מְדַיְּנֵנוּ has a dagesh in the yod.
יִזְכָּר: the qamats under the kaf is as printed.
מַגִּיד: the mark under the mem could be qamats rather than pataḥ.
דָּבָר: both vowels look like qamats in the print (the usual reading is דְּבַר). I left this as printed.
חק: I can't see a ḥolam in the scan.
לַאֲדֹנֵינוּ is defective (no vav), while the earlier אֲדוֹנֵינוּ is plene.
יוֹצִיא: the final alef is a large or ornamental glyph at the line end. It is the same letter, not an extra mark.
I left out any mark at the end of the line on הַמִּשְׁפָּט.

blocks.text: פותחים הארון. חזן. ע״ס א״ב כפול. קהל.
uncertainties: The rubric is in small unpointed type. 'חזן.' sits over the right-hand (first) column and 'קהל.' over the left-hand (response) column. 'ע״ס א״ב כפול' is a note on the double alphabetic acrostic.

blocks.text: הָאוֹחֵז בְּיַד מִדַּת מִשְׁפָּט: וְכֹל מַאֲמִינִים שֶׁהוּא אֵל אֱמוּנָה:
uncertainties: בְּיַד: the vowel under the yod could be qamats.
וְכֹל: the ḥolam is faint.

blocks.text: הַבּוֹחֵן וּבוֹדֵק גִּנְזֵי נִסְתָּרוֹת: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא בּוֹחֵן כְּלָיוֹת:
uncertainties: In every following line, the response cue וְ״מַ is the printed short form of וְכֹל מַאֲמִינִים. I kept it as a cue and did not expand it. I can't confirm the pataḥ under the מ on every line.

blocks.text: הַגּוֹאֵל מִמָּוֶת וּפוֹדֶה מִשַּׁחַת: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא גּוֹאֵל חָזָק:
הַדָּן יְחִידִי לְבָאֵי עוֹלָם: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא דַּיַּן אֱמֶת:
uncertainties: There is a stray dot after לְבָאֵי, probably a scan artifact.
דַּיַּן: the second vowel could be qamats.

blocks.text: הֶהָגוּי בְּאֶהְיֶה אֲשֶׁר אֶהְיֶה: וְמַ״ שֶׁהָיָה (וְהֹוֶה) וְיִהְיֶה:
uncertainties: On this line the cue is set differently: the gershayim come after the מ (looks like וּמַ״) and touch שֶׁהָיָה. The vowel under the ו is unclear.
(וְהֹוֶה) is a printed parenthetical alternative.

blocks.text: הַוַּדַּי שְׁמוֹ כֵּן תְּהִלָּתוֹ: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא וְאֵין בִּלְתּוֹ:
uncertainties: הַוַּדַּי looks like it has no alef, unlike the common הַוַּדַּאי. The dagesh in the dalet is unclear.

blocks.text: הַזּוֹכֵר לְמַזְכִּירָיו טוֹבוֹת זִכְרוֹנוֹת: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא זוֹכֵר הַבְּרִית:
הַחוֹתֵךְ חַיִּים לְכָל־חָי: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא חַי וְקַיָּם:
הַטּוֹב וּמֵטִיב לָרָעִים וְלַטּוֹבִים: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא טוֹב לַכֹּל:
uncertainties: The ḥolam in לַכֹּל is faint.

blocks.text: הַיּוֹדֵעַ יֵצֶר כָּל יְצוּרִים: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא יוֹצְרָם בַּבָּטֶן:
הַכֹּל יוֹכָל וְכֹלְלָם יַחַד: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא כֹּל יוֹכָל:
uncertainties: וְכֹלְלָם: the vowels under the lameds are unclear.
יַחַד: the first vowel could be qamats.
כֹּל in the response: the ḥolam is not clearly visible.

blocks.text: הַלָּן בְּסֵתֶר בְּצֵל, שַׁדַּי: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא לְבַדּוֹ הוּא:
uncertainties: The comma before שַׁדַּי is printed.

blocks.text: הַמַּמְלִיךְ מְלָכִים וְלוֹ הַמְּלוּכָה: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא מֶלֶךְ עוֹלָם:
הַנּוֹהֵג בְּחַסְדּוֹ כָּל־דּוֹר: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא נוֹצֵר חֶסֶד:
הַסּוֹבֵל וּמַעֲלִים עַיִן מִסּוֹרְרִים: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא סוֹלֵחַ סֶלָה:
uncertainties: וּמַעְלִים: under the ע I can't tell sheva from ḥataf-pataḥ.
מִסּוֹרְרִים: the first ר could have ḥataf-pataḥ rather than sheva.

blocks.text: הָעֶלְיוֹן, וְעֵינוֹ אֶל יְרֵאָיו: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא עוֹנֶה לָחַשׁ:
uncertainties: There is a small stray mark under עוֹנֶה, probably an artifact.

blocks.text: One is our God, He is our father, He is our king, He is our helper; He will again let us hear in His mercy before the eyes of all the living: ‘To be God unto you’.
I am the Lord your God.
O Mighty One, our Mighty One, O Lord, our Lord, how mighty is Thy Name over the whole earth. The Lord will be King over the whole earth, on that day will the Lord be One and His Name One.

The fame of Thine honour makes Thee feared upon the whole earth. When Thou didst make judgment heard from heaven, the earth shook before it returned to its rest. Before the storm on the day of judgment, the floods of the earth roared. There was a mighty Shofar blast, then the Lord spoke and called to the earth, the end of the earth proclaimed the beauty of the righteous God in a song of praise. Fear, fright, dread and terror will then take hold of the earth when Thou arisest for judgment, to show anger with all the ends of the earth. ‘Make straight, clear the way’ those who tremble at the earth’s shaking will say. O luminous and mighty One, Thou wilt reassure the earth: ‘what do you fear, O earth, let the depths of the earth rejoice’.
That it may be known and revealed that He is King over the whole earth; just as He was always praised in heaven, so shall His tested ones acquire the right to praise Him on earth.
O Mighty One, our Mighty One, O Lord, our Lord, how mighty is Thy Name over the whole earth. The Lord will be King over the whole earth, on that day will the Lord be One and His Name One.
And in Thy holy words it is written saying:
The Lord will reign in eternity, your God, O Zion, from generation to generation, Halleluyah.

From generation to generation we will proclaim Thy greatness and for all eternity sanctify Thy holiness. Thy praise, O our God, shall not depart from our mouth for ever and ever, for Thou art God, a great and holy King.

For those who sanctify Thee, hast Thou sanctified with Thy holiness. Glorification by holy ones is becoming to the Holy One. Therefore, let Thy Name, O Lord our God, be sanctified over Israel Thy people, over Jerusalem, Thy city,

over Zion the dwelling of Thy glory, over the kingdom of the house of David Thine anointed, and over Thy residence and Thy sanctuary. Our Lord will yet remember on our behalf the love of the immortal (Abraham), and for the sake of the son (Isaac) who let himself be bound for the sacrifice, He will make an end of our accusers, and through the merit of the innocent (Jacob) will the Awe-inspiring One pronounce our righteous verdict for this day is holy to our Lord. When no defender confronts the accuser, Thou wilt pronounce for Jacob statute and judgment, justify us then in judgment, O King of judgment.
In His hand He holds the attribute of judgment. All believe that He is God of faith.
He tests and examines hidden secrets. All believe that He tests the inwards.
He redeems from death and delivers from destruction. All believe that He is a strong redeemer.
He judges alone those who come into the world. All believe that He is judge of truth.
He is thought of as ‘I am that I am’. All believe that He was, is and shall be.
Sure is His Name and likewise His fame. All believe that He is with none beside Him.
He remembers those who remember Him in kind memory. All believe that He remembers the covenant.
He distributes life to all the living. All believe that He lives and endures.
He is good and acts well towards evil and good. All believe that He is good towards all.
He knows the impulse of all creatures. All believe that He has formed them in the womb.
He has power over all and contains them all. All believe that He has power over all.
Almighty, He dwells in mystery, in shadow. All believe that He alone is He.
He appoints kings and His is the kingdom. All believe that He is King of the world.
He leads with His mercy every generation. All believe that He retains kindness.
He is long suffering and hides His eye from the stubborn. All believe that He grants pardon.
He is supreme and His eye rests on those who fear Him. All believe that He answers soft prayer.
